chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: Resonator guitar and acoustic guitar on Honey Keep Your Mind on Me
summary: Honey, Keep Your Mind on Me was acoustic; earlier he used a resonator guitar with a tin piece and mike, giving a bottle-like electrified sound.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, what were you playing on -- when you got the (inaudible), what sort of guitar were you playing on that?
Well, Honey, Keep Your Mind On Me was accoustic guitar.
Yeah.
But further back, I was using a -- I think I had a resonator.
Well, now, when you say a resonator, what --
That guitar has a big resonator, a piece of tin built in it, and it would be --
Oh, I see, yeah.
-- with little holes in it.
So that really wasn't electric.
No. But once I put the mike to it, it was sounding like electric, and loud, too.
Oh, I got you.
That's how I got that funny sound, like hitting a bottle.
Yeah, yeah.

Then, maybe hitting a bottle, because those wasn't like the guitars -- they wasn't perfecting it at that time. But it's the same thing, if I'd hook up into this and put this into the guitar and it'd come to the speaker.
Yeah, yeah.
So that's only different rhythms.
So this was -- I mean, this whole thing of resonators and everything was a matter of making the guitar sort of audible, so people could hear it.
Yeah, it would, and sound electrified, too.
Yeah.
Yeah.
